title: Freya and the Vow
premise: Casper Vasquez, a jaded wedding planner who swore off love after her own engagement collapsed, is roped into her firm's charity pen-pal program and assigned an anonymous correspondent: 'F.' Their letters crack her open — until she discovers F is Freya Lindqvist, the icy heiress whose society wedding Casper is planning, and who is marrying for duty to save her family's estate. As the letters deepen into something neither can deny, Freya must choose between the inheritance that anchors her family and a truth that would unravel everything, while Casper must risk loving wholeheartedly instead of in fragments. On the wedding day, with the vows half-written, Freya speaks a different vow aloud — and Casper, holding the final letter, answers it.
about_author: Quentin Lockridge is the pseudonym of a former event coordinator who spent a decade behind the scenes of other people's weddings before turning those observations into fiction. Writing from a coastal town where lighthouses outnumber traffic lights, Lockridge specializes in romances about people who insist they are done with love.

chapters.title: The Planner Who Doesn't Believe
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She orchestrates a flawless wedding for strangers who barely look at each other, then goes home to a drawer of unsent letters from her ex-fiancé. Her boss announces the firm's new charity pen-pal initiative and volunteers everyone. Emotional beat: weary professionalism masking grief; Casper agrees only to avoid questions.

chapters.title: Dear Anonymous
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Casper's first letter is sarcastic; the reply she receives is formal, clipped, oddly vulnerable at the edges. Freya, writing from Lindqvist House under a pseudonym, treats the assignment as an obligation until Casper's honesty startles a confession out of her: she is engaged to a man she does not love. Beat: two guarded women accidentally telling the truth.

chapters.title: The Lindqvist Account
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The firm lands its biggest commission of the year: the Lindqvist-Harrow wedding at a crumbling ancestral estate. Casper meets Freya in person — cold, precise, dismissive — and dislikes her instantly, never suspecting her correspondent's identity. Beat: dramatic irony tightens; attraction flickers beneath friction.

chapters.title: What the Letters Know
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Planning sessions with Casper are combative, but Freya finds herself describing them in her next letter almost tenderly. She realizes with horror that her anonymous friend and her planner share the same dry wit, the same scarred view of love. Beat: suspicion blooms; Freya tests Casper with a detail from the letters.

chapters.title: Rain on the Terrace
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A storm strands them together reviewing floor plans; an argument about 'real' weddings turns personal, and they nearly kiss before Freya retreats. That night, both write letters confessing they've met someone who unsettles them. Beat: desire acknowledged obliquely, duty invoked as armor.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya's grandmother's will requires her marriage to secure the estate; her fiancé Harrow knows and holds it over her. When he discovers her letters, he threatens exposure. Freya must end the correspondence — or lose everything. Beat: loyalty to family weaponized against truth; Freya sends a cold goodbye letter.

chapters.title: Pieces of a Heart
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Reeling from the abrupt silence of her pen pal and snubbed by Freya at a fitting, Casper recognizes the parallel too late — the handwriting on a contract matches the letters. Confronting Freya privately, she gets a denial she doesn't believe. Beat: betrayal, anger, and the terrifying admission that she cares anyway.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wedding week descends; Harrow grows openly controlling, and Freya goes through rehearsal like a sleepwalker. Casper, bound by contract, watches the woman she loves rehearse vows built on a clause. A near-miss: Freya slips and quotes a line from their letters aloud. Beat: dread rising toward breaking point.

chapters.title: The Vow Interrupted
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax. At the ceremony, as Freya reaches 'I do,' Casper steps forward with the final letter Freya never sent — returned unopened by Harrow as cruelty. Reading it aloud was his threat; Casper makes it a gift instead. Freya speaks her true vow, renouncing the inheritance terms publicly. Beat: ruin and liberation in one breath.

chapters.title: Everything After Yes
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, coda. Months later: the estate saved through Freya's lawsuit and a heritage trust, the wedding business reimagined around honest ceremonies, and one small wedding planned perfectly — their own. Casper writes a letter she delivers by hand. Beat: love in present tense at last; the vow kept, not spoken.
